entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Christopher Lekapenos or Lecapenus was the eldest son of Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos and co-emperor of the Byzantine Empire from 921 until his death in 931. Christopher was given the position of megas hetaireiarches in spring 919, after Romanos assumed guardianship of the underage Emperor Constantine VII. Romanos, who made himself co-emperor in 920, raised Christopher to co-emperor on 21 May 921 to give his family precedence over Constantine VII's Macedonian line. In 928 Christopher's father-in-law, Niketas, unsuccessfully attempted to incite Christopher to usurp his father, resulting in Niketas being banished.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As co-emperor alongside Constantine VII, Christopher Lekapenos played a crucial role in maintaining imperial stability and power during a tumultuous period of Byzantine history. His reign marked the beginning of the Macedonian dynasty's resurgence.
